title: Grade 4 ELA — How Informational Text Is Organized
subject: English Language Arts
description: Practice with questions on sequence, comparison, cause and effect, problem and solution.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: We left at dawn. By noon we reached the falls. We returned at sunset. How are the details arranged?
Too much rain filled the creek. As a result, the bridge path flooded. How does the author connect events?
Both foxes and coyotes eat small animals. Coyotes are usually larger than foxes. What structure does the writer use?
The class kept losing its paint brushes. It solved the problem by labeling a cup for each table. Which structure fits?
A moth has two pairs of wings. Its wings are covered in tiny scales. What does the author mainly do?
choices: show how to build a wing

questions.question: First unplug the device. Next wipe it with a dry cloth. Finally, let it sit before plugging it in. Which structure helps the reader use this text?
The strings of the instruments looked alike. Unlike the violin, the cello rests on the floor while it is played. Which word signals a difference?
Because a pipe burst, the gym floor became wet. Which part names the cause?
choices: the floor was in a gym

questions.question: The lights near the bridge failed. The town installed new ones to make the crossing easier to see. Which detail tells the solution?
choices: The crossing was hard to see.

questions.question: The lights near the bridge failed. The town installed new ones to make the crossing easier to see. Which heading best fits a compare-and-contrast article?
choices: How Moths and Butterflies Are Alike and Different

questions.question: The lights near the bridge failed. The town installed new ones to make the crossing easier to see. Which organizer best shows two similarities and two differences?
The lights near the bridge failed. The town installed new ones to make the crossing easier to see. Which word often signals that an effect follows?
The lights near the bridge failed. The town installed new ones to make the crossing easier to see. Which sentence signals the last action in a procedure?
choices: Unlike bees, wasps have a smooth body.
Because the lid was gone, the paint dried.

questions.question: In May, crews repaired the trail. In July, they rebuilt the bridge. In October, they painted signs. Why did the author include months?
choices: to explain why a sign is blue
to help show when each event happened

questions.question: Spruce trees keep needles through winter. Maple trees typically lose their leaves in fall. What information might best complete this comparison?
choices: how both kinds of trees make and use seeds
how to bake a loaf of bread

questions.question: When salt was spread, some ice melted. Meltwater ran toward a drain. What effect was linked to adding salt?
Cracks in the sidewalk tripped walkers. Workers filled the cracks with a firm patch. What is the problem?
A ladybug has a round body, a spotted outer shell, and small legs. Why is description a useful structure here?
choices: It proves two animals are alike.
It helps the reader picture the ladybug.
It lists the order of steps.

questions.question: We sorted the rocks. Next we labeled the types. Last we put the groups on display. Which event came between sorting and displaying the rocks?
Both routes reach the pond. Trail A is short but steep. Trail B is long but flat. Why might the writer compare the routes?
choices: to help hikers choose a route
to list what happened on a hike
to describe what lives in the water
to explain why the pond froze
